subject: Dedicated capacity term mix and soft-start cadence — GPU pool structuring
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novacorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@novacorp.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool — timing & term questions

Jonas,

Thanks for taking the time on the call today. A quick follow-up from the SRE side: we are looking at a committed dedicated pool for inference (customer-facing web queries + nightly batch jobs). Two big unknowns for us are the start date flexibility and how you price blended terms if we want a 12-month guaranteed base with a 24/36 month discount ladder on bumped capacity. Rough sketch: baseline 8 A100-equivalent GPUs guaranteed, up to 32 for bursts over a 6-8 week ramp. Can Redwood support a soft start (lower guaranteed throughput for month 1–2 while we validate traffic) and then a hard commitment effective month 3?

Also: what are the discount breakpoints for 12/24/36? We need to present a proposal to procurement by next Tuesday.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Morales
VP, Platform Engineering — NovaCorp

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — timing & term questions

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a soft-start cadence and a blended-term pricing schedule; we commonly model a 60-day validation window before the full guaranteed throughput takes effect. Below is a proposal outline (I will attach a PDF with the numbers):

- Baseline guaranteed pool: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (12-month guaranteed term)
- Soft-start: months 0–2 at 50% throughput guarantee (i.e., billing applies to 4 GPUs level of guarantee), full guarantee starts month 3
- Burst: up to 32 GPUs available for bursts; bursts billed at on-demand pricing with capped burst-hours per month (default 1,200 GPU-hours), can be increased with an add-on.
- Term discounts (indicative): 12-month = baseline price; 24-month = ~12% off baseline; 36-month = ~20% off baseline. Discounts apply to the guaranteed-commit portion only, burst/on-demand rates separate.
- Trigger for ramp: hard start (month 3) can be set to a calendar date or volume trigger (e.g., sustained 10% above baseline for two consecutive weeks).
- SLA: 99.9%% uptime on dedicated pool, with credits for missed availability; additional throughput guarantees available for higher-tier commits.

I'll have Marissa and Ben include a month-by-month invoice cadence and sample amortization schedule in the attached. If you want the legal/contract language to reflect a conditional start (i.e., full commitment only after acceptance of production test plan), we can add that as a clause.

I'll follow up with the formal proposal within 24 hours.

— Jonas
Lead Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated GPU pool — pricing details & ramping (internal notes)

Jonas / Ben — internal read: Elena asked for procurement-ready numbers and explicit checkpoints. Key negotiation levers we can use: overall term length (24 vs 36), milestone invoice structure, staging credits for months 0–2, and adding a migration/validation SLA to limit their exposure.

My suggestions:
- Offer a 24-month preferred package at 15% off baseline if they sign within 2 weeks. 36-month stays at 20% but requires commit to a minimum 75%% of baseline utilization after month 6.
- Include a 60-day soft-start where we cap guaranteed billing at 50%% but provide a one-time credit equal to 25%% of months 0–2 charges if the customer meets the validation checklist (so they get partial protection).
- For bursts: include 800 guaranteed burst-hours per month at a 30%% discount to on-demand, additional burst-hours billed at standard on-demand.
- Add a clause: if they expand guaranteed capacity by >50%% within first 12 months, we re-evaluate pricing (simple upward adjustment).

Attachments: I prepared two artifacts — a pricing grid and a draft SLA matrix (see attached filenames).

Marissa
Director, Revenue — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated GPU pool — pricing details & ramping (internal notes)

Quick note on procurement flags: procurement will want clear termination and migration costs. Recommend we propose a phased invoice schedule to soften cashflow ask: 40% on signing, 30% at hard start (month 3), 30% spread evenly across remaining months. For the soft-start credit, better to show it as a conditional credit line item (so it does not complicate revenue recognition).

Also, suggest we set a firm start date option (e.g., 2026-11-01) with the alternative of a trigger-based start no later than 2027-01-01. That gives NovaCorp scheduling predictability and a fallback.

Ben
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novacorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, ops@novacorp.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — timing & term questions

Jonas / Marissa / Ben — thanks, this is very close to what procurement wants. A few clarifications before we go to legal:

1) Can we get the 24-month 15%% discount in writing with the soft-start credit included (we accept the conditional 75%% utilization clause for 36-month but prefer 24-month now).
2) Please confirm the exact throughput guarantee measurement: requests/sec at p95 latency <= 200ms for our typical 512-token prompt profile. If that needs an add-on, call it out.
3) On billing: the phased schedule Ben proposed works. We will ask for a cap on monthly burst spend (suggest $45k) to avoid surprises — please confirm whether you can enforce throwing bursts into a spend cap versus pure on-demand billing.

If you can send a procurement-ready PDF with the clauses and a DocuSign link by COB Monday, we'll route to legal.

— Elena
VP, Platform Engineering — NovaCorp
